MIT has engineered a tiny flying microrobot that weighs less than a paper clip and achieves independent flight. 

This miniature robot flaps its wings 330 times per second using an onboard chip and three sensors to navigate without external cameras. It represents a significant jump in autonomous micro aerial vehicles, demonstrating how advanced robotics can function without being tethered to a motion capture system. 

Engineers and robotics enthusiasts will appreciate how this autonomous flying robot maintains stability while carrying its own brain. The hardware design shows how far we have come in creating insect-sized technology that can operate in the real world. 

This breakthrough highlights the future of small-scale autonomous flight. Subscribe for weekly tech and robotics breakdowns, and let me know in the comments if you think these tiny bots will eventually be used for search and rescue.
